questions.q: Per this lesson, what is now the only supported declarative automation tool on the Salesforce platform?
options: Workflow Rules
Process Builder
Flow Builder
Apex triggers
questions.explain: Workflow Rules and Process Builder reached end of support, leaving Flow Builder as the only supported declarative automation tool, which the lesson gives as one reason to default to Flow.

questions.q: What are the two entry criteria for the Case to Installation Job Flow?
options: Case.Type is Installation or Repair, and Case.AssetId is not null
Case.Status is Closed and Case.Priority is High
Case.Owner is a Service Manager and Case.Subject contains 'repair'
Case.CreatedDate is today and Case.Type is any value
questions.explain: The Flow's entry criteria fires only when the Case's type is Installation or Repair and it has an Asset linked, so it doesn't run on every Case edit.

questions.q: Why is technician assignment built as a separate subflow rather than inline in the main Flow?
options: Subflows run faster than inline logic
So it can be reused if Solstice adds another entry point that also needs technician assignment
Flow Builder does not allow assignment logic inline
Because subflows are required for every Flow regardless of reuse
questions.explain: The lesson explains the subflow is built specifically for reuse -- if another part of the org later needs the same assignment logic, it can call the same subflow.

questions.q: According to the governing rule from Lesson 2, why does the Case to Installation Job automation belong in Flow rather than an Apex trigger?
options: Because Flow is always faster than Apex
Because Apex cannot read Case records
Because Flow cannot call subflows
Because the logic is likely to change for business reasons and an admin should be able to adjust it without redeploying code
questions.explain: The test given is whether the logic is likely to change for business reasons an admin should be able to adjust directly -- which is true here, unlike the warranty-claim validation reserved for Apex.

questions.q: What specifically happens if the Create Records element in this Flow has no fault path and the create fails?
options: The Case saves successfully with no visible indication that the Installation Job silently failed to create
The Case fails to save entirely
The Flow automatically retries the create three times
Salesforce sends an automatic email to every user in the org
questions.explain: Without a fault path, a failure in Create Records can leave the Case saved with no job created and no visible signal -- exactly the invisible failure the fault path's Case Comment is meant to prevent.
